rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:passivity``: Keep passive-sourced legs author-attributed, target-fixed and immutable; refuse autonomous passive-node emission, which injects routing connections no actor consented to or authored.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:tensor-format
rows.statement: Preserve the distinct full slice and extracted path-view matrix interfaces.

rows.label: case:necessity:tensor-format-scalar-routing
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:tensor-format``: Keep the stored 3 by 3 slice and extracted 2 by 2 path view for their distinct consumers; refuse routing on a single derived scalar, which loses orientation, matrix composition and the separation of routing discrimination from attribution equity, even if the parameters remain auditable.

rows.label: case:necessity:tensor-format-lossy-storage
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:tensor-format``: Keep the non-lossy parameter declaration so scoring objects can be recomputed; refuse storing only a derived scalar and discarding the parameters, which breaks auditability. This storage failure requires parameter sufficiency, not by itself the tensor format.

rows.label: rem:necessity:tensor-overdetermination-convenience
rows.statement: Treat cached-slice consistency as a diagnostic rather than provenance.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:average-based-aggregation
rows.statement: Retain the declared terminal mean fold rather than unbounded parameter summation.

rows.label: case:necessity:average-based-aggregation-summation
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:average-based-aggregation``: Keep arithmetic-mean aggregation; refuse summing sentiment parameters, which drives repeated identical contributions into clamp saturation and erases per-actor sentiment magnitude rather than preserving parameter fidelity.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:per-author-netting
rows.statement: Net complete authored coordinates within the declared bundle and exclude derived/control/settlement readings.

rows.label: case:necessity:per-author-netting-weight-netting
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:per-author-netting``: Keep full-incidence, per-author parameter netting by sum-then-clip to [-1,1] for endorsement projection only; refuse summing already transformed edge weights, which can exceed the published path-weight ceilings.

rows.label: case:necessity:per-author-netting-cross-author-netting
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:per-author-netting``: Keep full-incidence bundles separate by author and net their parameters only; refuse cross-author netting, which lets one author’s revision cancel another author’s live consent through a shared passive node.

rows.label: case:necessity:per-author-netting-derived-bond-netting
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:per-author-netting``: Keep derived Self-edge components outside record netting and recompute their activation from final standing; refuse netting them as records, a category error because they have no authored bundle and their responsive channel is not an accumulated record quantity.

rows.label: case:necessity:per-author-netting-settlement-netting
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:per-author-netting``: Keep settlement records outside endorsement-only parameter netting; refuse netting them, which hides the individual records settlement recognition reads.

rows.label: case:necessity:per-author-netting-control-netting
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:per-author-netting``: Keep control records outside endorsement-only parameter netting; refuse netting them, which hides the individual control records settlement recognition reads.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:max-product-path-scoring
rows.statement: Keep raw maximum-path traversal distinct from a sum-of-paths estimator.

rows.label: case:necessity:max-product-path-scoring-sum-of-paths
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:max-product-path-scoring``: Keep max-product path scoring; refuse summing over all paths, which lets k parallel paths multiply the score by k and turns internal redundancy into manufactured visibility.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:conserved-rival-allocation
rows.statement: Normalize allocation across self and all recipients to one conserved unit.

rows.label: case:necessity:conserved-rival-allocation-independent-weights
rows.statement: Independent per-pair weights without a row budget permit cost-free replication of regard; row conservation instead makes intact source pairs rival and preserves the closed weighted mean. Endorsing everyone is not equivalent to endorsing no one for coordinates or maxima. Under ``thm:epoch:split-observational-equivalence``, a record-based remedy imposes the same change on a legitimate completion with identical public fields, or the same distribution of changes if randomized.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:self-retention-base
rows.statement: Keep a positive unmodulated self base and retain unallocated pair mass.

rows.label: case:necessity:self-retention-base-drop-mass
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:self-retention-base``: Keep unallocated source mass as positive self-retention; refuse dropping it, which lowers row sums below one and breaks the equality between a closed cluster’s weighted mean and its ledger ratio.

rows.label: case:necessity:self-retention-base-tilt-self
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:self-retention-base``: Keep self-retention unmodulated by standing; refuse tilting the self share, which lets standing defend its own retention without a new source or act and introduces a direct feedback channel.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:domain-weighted-allocation
rows.statement: Sum weighted act coefficients with one normalized domain profile per act.

rows.label: case:necessity:domain-weighted-allocation-domain-double-counting
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:domain-weighted-allocation``: Keep published domain weights and a normalized domain profile summing to one for each folded act contribution; refuse counting an act once per projected domain, which lets its shape multiply the same authored intent for the same debit.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:finite-depth-conserved-transport
rows.statement: Use the published finite supported-depth mixture.

rows.label: case:necessity:finite-depth-conserved-transport-unbounded-closure
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:finite-depth-conserved-transport``: Keep one conserved transport operator mixed from a published finite depth mass; refuse unbounded transitive closure, which has no finite deepest-supported-depth screen and expands contributing width to the whole graph’s rate range.

rows.label: case:necessity:finite-depth-conserved-transport-single-hop
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:finite-depth-conserved-transport``: Keep the published finite-depth transport mixture; refuse replacing it with a single hop, which reports only immediate allocation and loses whether allocating sources are themselves backed, making the comparator purely local.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:hop-faded-responsive-tilt
rows.statement: Attach hop exponents to transported mass rather than authored rows.

rows.label: case:necessity:hop-faded-responsive-tilt-flat-profile
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:hop-faded-responsive-tilt``: Keep a hop-decaying tilt profile owned by transported mass; refuse a flat profile, whose two-sided volume grows with the hop count instead of the front-loaded sum and fails the prior screen at twice the cap.

rows.label: case:necessity:hop-faded-responsive-tilt-row-owned-exponent
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:hop-faded-responsive-tilt``: Keep the tilt exponent attached to transported mass at its own hop index; refuse a row-owned exponent, since one row relaying both its own and a distant source’s mass would need two exponents in one product, invalidating the propagation argument.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:epoch-set-standing
rows.statement: Exclude previous standing and incidental intraepoch order from the mathematical result.

rows.label: case:necessity:epoch-set-standing-order-input
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:epoch-set-standing``: Keep standing a function of the completed epoch set and final-state inputs; refuse intra-epoch order as a standing input, which lets a host reorder concurrent acts to move a verdict without a recorded semantic choice. Formation and order-sensitive raw quantities still read authoritative order.

rows.label: case:necessity:epoch-set-standing-memory-input
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:epoch-set-standing``: Keep standing memoryless on the completed epoch inputs; refuse the preceding epoch’s standing as a semantic input, which makes the answer path-dependent and prevents holders of the same records from independently agreeing by replay.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:title-coupled-settlement-standing
rows.statement: Resolve unsettled settlement acts to self and recognized events to counterparties.

rows.label: case:necessity:title-coupled-settlement-standing-face-value
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:title-coupled-settlement-standing``: Keep settlement allocation coupled to the title fold: direct it to the counterparty only when settlement settled, otherwise to the author. Refuse weighing an asserted settlement at face value, which lets unauthorized or losing acts deliver directed allocation without completing a transfer.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:clamped-entry-bounds
rows.statement: Use the declared master-formula clamps and preserve zero-parameter routing degeneracy.

rows.label: case:necessity:clamped-entry-bounds-raw-products
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:clamped-entry-bounds``: Keep the master formula’s clamped entry bounds and polarization floor; refuse unclamped raw parameter products, which lose the floor and allow rank-one degeneracy and zero path-view determinant at weak or vanishing parameters.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:always-active-baseline
rows.statement: Retain the mask-independent full-slice baseline.

rows.label: case:necessity:always-active-baseline-drop-baseline
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:always-active-baseline``: Keep the always-active baseline entry as the mask-independent norm anchor; refuse dropping it, which makes the guaranteed floor depend on the mask. Full-mask entries still contribute at zero parameters, so baseline deletion alone does not make that full-mask norm zero.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:eta-softening
rows.statement: Use the declared bleed and derived Half-tier floor in path views.

rows.label: case:necessity:eta-softening-hard-zeroing
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:eta-softening``: Keep bleed-softening of masked path-view entries; refuse hard-zeroing, which makes the marginal restricted masks singular and their edges impassable even when the stored slice has nonzero norm.

rows.label: case:necessity:eta-softening-epistemic-zero
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:eta-softening``: Keep bleed-softening for the Epistemic path-view mask; refuse zeroing its masked column, which gives an identically zero determinant and infinite routing cost regardless of parameters.

rows.label: case:necessity:eta-softening-economic-zero
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:eta-softening``: Keep bleed-softening for the Economic path-view mask; refuse hard-zeroing its masked entries, which forces zero determinant.

rows.label: case:necessity:eta-softening-minimal-zero
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:eta-softening``: Keep bleed-softening for the Minimal path-view mask; refuse zeroing three of its four entries, which forces zero determinant and destroys routing through that mask.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:dual-view-architecture
rows.statement: Separate determinant routing from Frobenius attribution inputs.

rows.label: case:necessity:dual-view-architecture-frobenius-only
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:dual-view-architecture``: Keep path-view determinant and sign for routing and attribution-view Frobenius norm for CAN; refuse Frobenius-only scoring, which makes Tag and Opinion routing nearly equal and cannot distinguish orientation-preserving from orientation-reversing interactions.

rows.label: case:necessity:dual-view-architecture-determinant-only
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:dual-view-architecture``: Keep the distinct routing and attribution views; refuse determinant-only CAN attribution, which gives Tag-based compositions less credit than Opinion-based compositions of comparable information content and discriminates by tier instead of contribution quality.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing
rows.statement: Preserve signed raw traversal while flagging its obsolete standing role.

rows.label: case:necessity:positive-parity-routing-magnitude-only
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:positive-parity-routing``: Keep determinant signs and positive-path-parity filtering in the raw endorsement service; refuse magnitude-only routing, which treats a strong negative-parity path as coherent endorsement. Positive parity is necessary for that routing test, not sufficient for a standing vouch: coherent hostility still fails the separate local stance test.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:strict-transmission-decay
rows.statement: Inventory strict terminal composition attenuation.

rows.label: case:necessity:strict-transmission-decay-lossless
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:strict-transmission-decay``: Keep saturated transmission mean/(1+mean), strictly below one; refuse lossless transmission, which lets a one-child wrapper retain the child’s full credit even as its connection strength tends to zero, defeating depth decay.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:inverse-temperature
rows.statement: Keep the locked temperature declaration distinct from speculative adaptive calibration.

rows.label: case:necessity:inverse-temperature-free-temperature
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:inverse-temperature``: Keep the declared inverse-temperature anchor 2 ln 2; refuse treating it as a freely tuned post-deployment parameter, which moves the maturity crossover so moderate-maturity noise passes at low values or cross-cluster discovery is suppressed at high values.

rows.label: case:necessity:inverse-temperature-low-temperature
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:inverse-temperature``: Keep the declared inverse-temperature anchor 2 ln 2; the beta=1 comparison is a refused replacement because its shifted crossover amplifies moderate-maturity noise, including the stated prior-degree example.

rows.label: case:necessity:inverse-temperature-high-temperature
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:inverse-temperature``: Keep the declared inverse-temperature anchor 2 ln 2; the beta=2 comparison is a refused replacement because amplification requires very high prior degree and cross-cluster discovery becomes effectively impossible in the stated comparison.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:redundancy-correction
rows.statement: Treat overlap discount as a replaceable terminal preference; preserve nonduplication, depth decay, attenuation and context independence.

rows.label: case:necessity:redundancy-correction-ignore-overlap
rows.statement: Terminal preference under ``subsec:necessity:redundancy-correction``: The canonical terminal overlap ratio discounts shared upstream work. Setting it to one is an alternative preference, not a forbidden simplification or an admission violation: normalized dependency weights already average identical contributions rather than multiply them. A guild may replace the discount under its published rule while preserving depth decay, strict transmission attenuation and context independence.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:participation-floor
rows.statement: Keep numeraire, safety threshold, policy floor and derived effective floor distinct.

rows.label: case:necessity:participation-floor-coupled-price-policy
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:participation-floor``: Keep the reduced wall, structural floor and policy dial distinct, joined to burn amounts by the numeraire; refuse one coupled price-policy constant, which forces congestion policy to reprice survivors although the door and curve are separable.

rows.label: case:necessity:participation-floor-capacity-gate
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:participation-floor``: Keep the participation gate distinct from capacity; refuse forcing them to coincide, which collapses the two-gate architecture and turns the dimensionless policy barrier into a hard monetary scale.

rows.label: case:necessity:participation-floor-uncontrolled-host-dial
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:participation-floor``: Keep a published wall controller and structural floor separate from the discretionary policy dial; refuse one uncontrolled host dial, which permits a wall below its floor and turns every controller adjustment into a governance decision.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:floor-as-numeraire
rows.statement: Reduce burn amounts by a co-expressed numeraire for invariance under unit change; at fixed purchasing power a market price increase by a factor divides the numeric burn by that factor, without market-repricing invariance.

rows.label: case:necessity:floor-as-numeraire-unreduced-debit
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:floor-as-numeraire``: Keep burn-balance debits in burn units and reduced-pair debits at the reduced wall; refuse subtracting the burn-denominated threshold directly from reduced pairs, which mixes burn and action units instead of using the numeraire as their unique join.

rows.label: case:necessity:floor-as-numeraire-unreduced-bond
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:floor-as-numeraire``: Keep burn and standing reduced by the numeraire before they meet counts or the bond kernel’s literal one; refuse unreduced burn/count adjacency, whose hidden unit makes bond activation saturate under redenomination. Reduction is invariant under a unit change only when the numeraire is re-expressed too; it does not make market repricing invariant.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:nu-reduced-kernel
rows.statement: Reduce activation by numeraire rather than the policy door.

rows.label: case:necessity:nu-reduced-kernel-gate-reduction
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:nu-reduced-kernel``: Keep the bond kernel reduced by the numeraire, with the participation floor confined to gate, freeze and entry cost; refuse reducing by the gate’s burn image, which makes every policy-floor move reshape bond weights and coupled dynamics for actors who remain admitted.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:time-locked-non-burnable
rows.statement: Leave realization unit classes below the four-object burn interface.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:time-locked-non-redeemable
rows.statement: Leave realization redemption mechanisms outside the network model.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:three-step-settlement
rows.statement: Require buyer Ratify after seller Accept for settlement recognition.

rows.label: case:necessity:three-step-settlement-accept-commit
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:three-step-settlement``: Keep buyer Ratify after seller Accept as the authored commitment proposal, finalized at the boundary; refuse commit-at-Accept, which separates earlier buyer funding from seller commitment and permits stale terms to bind without the buyer’s current consent.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:explicit-cancels
rows.statement: Use authored cancellation rather than invented per-Bid timeouts.

rows.label: case:necessity:explicit-cancels-expiry
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:explicit-cancels``: Keep explicit authored, immutable Withdraw and Rescind records without per-object timeout; refuse per-Bid expiry, which causes an unrecorded state transition from unrelated throughput and violates causal locality.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:mutual-consumption
rows.statement: Consume all conflicting coepoch commits without permanently blocking the Item.

rows.label: case:necessity:mutual-consumption-order-tiebreak
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:mutual-consumption``: Keep conflicting co-epochal commits consumed without transfer while the incumbent retains title; refuse canonical-order tiebreaks, which re-import sub-epoch ordering authority into ownership.

rows.label: case:necessity:mutual-consumption-permanent-void
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:mutual-consumption``: Keep mutual consumption without transfer and leave the Item transferable; refuse permanent void, which lets a persistent tied pair block the thread forever and strand its accumulated history.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent
rows.statement: Let written cancellation through the committing epoch defeat transfer.

rows.label: case:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent-instant-commit
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent``: Keep consent live through the boundary, with a cancel in or before the Ratify epoch defeating commitment; refuse commit at the Ratify record instant, which requires a sub-epoch ordering authority to resolve cancel races.

rows.label: case:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent-arrival-order
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent``: Keep epoch-membership-based consent through the boundary; refuse operator-assigned arrival order as the cancel/commit tiebreak, which makes ownership depend on arrival accident and the operator’s ordering choice.

rows.label: case:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent-asserted-time
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:epoch-quantized-consent``: Keep epoch-membership-based consent through the boundary; refuse author-asserted times as the cancel/commit tiebreak, which admits time-stuffing and corrupts title.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:no-privileged-cancel-class
rows.statement: Apply ordinary gates and debit to cancellation acts.

rows.label: case:necessity:no-privileged-cancel-class-exempt-cancels
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:no-privileged-cancel-class``: Keep cancels under universal gates, ordinary closure and ordinary act pricing; refuse gate- or write-exempt control records, which create an unpriced append channel detached from the author’s dilution cost. Equal-epoch recognition favors cancels without granting them a write right.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:endogenous-clearing
rows.statement: Publish constraints and accepted-set validity without inventing normative optimal selection.

rows.label: case:necessity:endogenous-clearing-normative-selection
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:endogenous-clearing``: Keep published constraints, replayable dependent-set partition validity and discretionary selection; refuse a normative price-order or packing rule audited against all unwritten demand, since that demand is not a Layer-1 object and the supposed audit cannot verify the counterfactual selection.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:conflict-not-causal
rows.statement: Do not force concurrent conflicts into one causal dependent set.

rows.label: case:necessity:conflict-not-causal-conflict-grouping
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:conflict-not-causal``: Keep conflict protection as the written-side tie-favoring recognition rule plus the named boundary-censorship exposure; the dependent set is already its causal closure. Refuse co-transport grouping of concurrent cancels and commits, which would require cross-references or serialization that destroys the regret window.

rows.label: case:necessity:conflict-not-causal-mandatory-cross-reference
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:conflict-not-causal``: Keep conflict protection as the written-side tie-favoring recognition rule plus the named boundary-censorship exposure; the dependent set is already its causal closure. Refuse mandatory cancel-to-commit cross-references, which force a Rescind to cite Ratify or a Withdraw to cite a later Accept and let the counterparty outrun early regret.

rows.label: case:necessity:conflict-not-causal-serialization
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:conflict-not-causal``: Keep conflict protection as the written-side tie-favoring recognition rule plus the named boundary-censorship exposure; the dependent set is already its causal closure. Refuse a serialization choice function, which re-imports sub-epoch ordering authority and destroys the regret window.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:stance-marginal-reputation
rows.statement: Keep terminal experience stance distinct from determinant coherence.

rows.label: case:necessity:stance-marginal-reputation-parity-reputation
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:stance-marginal-reputation``: Keep commercial reputation on each settlement edge’s stance marginal and routing on bilinear parity; refuse parity for both, which makes a coerced-unfair Accept with two negative coordinates yield the same positive reputation sign as the best experience.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:universal-act-weighing
rows.statement: Allocate outward only for eligible positive coordinates while weighing other acts at self.

rows.label: case:necessity:universal-act-weighing-parity-only
rows.statement: Parity-only endorsement wrongly treats coherent hostility as an outward vouch like praise. A higher-rate source lifts under the frozen-flow comparison, but a completed act changes debit, count and allocation, so this counterfactual proves no universal act-induced lift. Changed-history displacement has the scoped pair and concentration bounds of ``prop:epoch:split-pair-displacement`` and ``prop:epoch:split-concentration``.

rows.label: case:necessity:universal-act-weighing-negative-weight
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:universal-act-weighing``: Keep nonnegative conserved allocation and resolve non-vouch acts home; refuse negative standing weights as a remedy for hostility, which destroys the convex-combination standing hull.

rows.label: case:necessity:universal-act-weighing-composed-stance
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:universal-act-weighing``: Keep stance as the local authored verdict deciding destination, with parity composing coherence; refuse composing stance along paths, which confuses local verdicts with orientation transport. A coherent hostile person-directed act remains weighed and resolves home.

rows.label: case:necessity:universal-act-weighing-exclude-hostility
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:universal-act-weighing``: Keep every act weighed, with hostile person-directed acts charged at full magnitude against their author’s conserved unit and resolved home; refuse excluding hostility from the weighing census, which discounts the author’s attack instead of pricing it.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:declarative-item-identity
rows.statement: Derive Item identity from genesis structure rather than erasable descriptions.

rows.label: case:necessity:declarative-item-identity-content-addressing
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:declarative-item-identity``: Keep Item identity as the genesis record’s structural key; refuse hashing its removable description as identity, which welds title to erasable bytes and makes removal orphan or re-key the title thread.

rows.label: case:necessity:declarative-item-identity-external-registry
rows.statement: An external referent registry imports an identity authority; declared Item identity remains distinct from the real-world referent question.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:handshake-actor-incidence
rows.statement: Retain direct Actor-to-Actor settlement incidence.

rows.label: case:necessity:handshake-actor-incidence-profile-handshake
rows.statement: Direct Actor incidence keeps title independent of Profile sentiment; recognition-blind raw routing remains separate from title-coupled counterparty standing.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:settlement-half-routing
rows.statement: Apply Half-tier path extraction to settlement families without changing stored blocks.

rows.label: case:necessity:settlement-half-routing-full-routing
rows.statement: Full-tier settlement is an alternative raw-view assignment, not an alternate standing or admission rule.

rows.label: case:necessity:settlement-half-routing-auction-gravity
rows.statement: Raw Bid discovery depends on surrounding graph and competition; a tier choice alone supplies no universal concentration bound.

rows.label: case:necessity:settlement-half-routing-endorsement-injection
rows.statement: Authored settlement incidence may be traversed without recognition only by the raw service. Half-tier demotion preserves determinant sign, not a universal scaling factor or negligible terminal exposure.

rows.label: case:necessity:settlement-half-routing-minimal-routing
rows.statement: The charter chooses Half-tier settlement routing; sign preservation proves neither a unique intermediate floor nor a quantitative deterrence guarantee.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:binary-join-request
rows.statement: Keep Join Request binary without fabricating recipient-authored incidence.

rows.label: case:necessity:binary-join-request-ternary-request
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:binary-join-request``: Keep Join Request binary from requester Actor to Chat; refuse a ternary request routed through the recipient Actor, which creates a recipient-sourced leg before that recipient authors anything and misrepresents their stance.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:invitation-profile-terminus
rows.statement: Require Invitation terminal incidence at the invitee Profile.

rows.label: case:necessity:invitation-profile-terminus-actor-terminus
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:invitation-profile-terminus``: Keep Invitation/T directed to the invitee’s Profile; refuse an Actor terminus, which creates another passive-sourced in-edge family and bypasses the standing-dependent Reputation funnel with an undamped conduit to fresh accounts.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:proposal-half-tier
rows.statement: Apply Half-tier routing to Join Request and Invitation A legs.

rows.label: case:necessity:proposal-half-tier-full-routing
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:proposal-half-tier``: Keep Join Request and Invitation/A at Half-tier routing; refuse Full-tier proposal routing, which gives unanswered proposals enacted-relation force and lets mass invitations manufacture Chat-adjacent visibility at proposal cost.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:unrestricted-departure
rows.statement: Do not add membership or authority predicates to Leave and De-invite formation.

rows.label: case:necessity:unrestricted-departure-leave-membership-check
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:unrestricted-departure``: Keep Leave admission under the universal write rule without a membership precondition; refuse rejecting a nonmember’s Leave, which makes terminal membership a binding admission predicate and suppresses a priced public dissociation.

rows.label: case:necessity:unrestricted-departure-deinvite-authority-check
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:unrestricted-departure``: Keep De-invite admission under the universal write rule without authority or target-membership preconditions; refuse those checks, which make membership binding and turn who may expel into a Layer-1 authority verdict instead of terminal guild policy.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:control-self-retention
rows.statement: Weigh every control act at its author and never as an outward vouch.

rows.label: case:necessity:control-self-retention-outward-control
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:control-self-retention``: Keep type-fixed control acts weighed and resolved to their author in every quadrant; refuse outward allocation merely because their fixed coordinates are positive and their raw tier is small, which turns De-invite into a vouch for the expellee rather than authored stance.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:deinvite-profile-terminus
rows.statement: Require De-invite terminal incidence at the target Profile.

rows.label: case:necessity:deinvite-profile-terminus-actor-terminus
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:deinvite-profile-terminus``: Keep De-invite/T directed to the target Profile; refuse an Actor terminus, which breaks the sole passive-sourced Reputation funnel and opens an undamped attention conduit. The conduit is feed-only: the control act still resolves home for standing.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:bridge-per-edge-positivity
rows.statement: Inventory positive-edge affinity as terminal bridge policy.

rows.label: case:necessity:bridge-per-edge-positivity-endpoint-parity
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:bridge-per-edge-positivity``: Keep affinity on the per-edge positive subgraph; refuse endpoint-parity-only filtering for that channel, which admits paired interior inversions and prices delivery to an interior consumer receiving an inverted signal.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:bridge-consent-difference
rows.statement: Inventory Profile-register consent while flagging the omitted direct-stance veto.

rows.label: case:necessity:bridge-consent-difference-positive-only
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:bridge-consent-difference``: Keep consent as the clipped positive-minus-negative register difference at the bridge Profile; refuse the positive register alone, which makes advertiser-authored dislike invisible to that consent comparison.

rows.label: case:necessity:bridge-consent-difference-actor-register
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:bridge-consent-difference``: Keep the consent register read at the bridge Profile; refuse reading it at the Actor, which traverses the Reputation component again after affinity already includes it, double-counting reputation and biasing bridge selection.

rows.label: case:necessity:bridge-consent-difference-ratio
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:bridge-consent-difference``: Keep the always-defined clipped register difference at the bridge Profile; refuse the positive/negative register ratio, which is undefined in the common zero-negative-register case.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:bridge-self-exclusion
rows.statement: Inventory advertiser exclusion from terminal target and bridge domains.

rows.label: case:necessity:bridge-self-exclusion-self-target
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:bridge-self-exclusion``: Keep the advertiser outside the target domain; refuse self-targeting, which prices a circuit back to the advertiser without external audience value. Under the excluded self-target case the target set is empty and reward is zero.

rows.label: case:necessity:bridge-self-exclusion-self-bridge
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:bridge-self-exclusion``: Keep the advertiser outside the bridge domain; refuse self-bridging, which lets an advertiser author its own endorsement factor and manufacture a self-endorsement circuit without a counterparty.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:edge-ontology
rows.statement: Avoid first-class node writes and authored boundary bonds; reconcile edge wording with act ownership.

rows.label: case:necessity:edge-ontology-node-records
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:edge-ontology``: Keep edge records and implicit node folds; refuse a second plane of first-class node records and attributes, which introduces new mutability, custody and erasure semantics and reopens genesis authorization and admission.

rows.label: case:necessity:edge-ontology-appended-bonds
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:edge-ontology``: Keep Layer-1 bond readings derived rather than appended; refuse Layer-1-authored bond records, which re-enter the admission set and reopen the append exception and epoch cascade.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:universal-parallelism
rows.statement: Preserve parallel authored acts without implicit merges or supersession.

rows.label: case:necessity:universal-parallelism-uniqueness-constraint
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:universal-parallelism``: Keep all record families parallelizable with no Layer-1 merge or supersession; refuse one-record-per-author/target or per-actor uniqueness constraints, which pull per-family state machines into admission and destroy the parallel accumulation needed for priced walk-back.

rows.label: case:necessity:universal-parallelism-latest-wins
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:universal-parallelism``: Keep binding standing and title bundle readings distinct from terminal consumers’ fold choices; refuse Layer-1 latest-wins everywhere, which repeals sum-then-clip, makes stance free to flip and imposes one fold on consumers with different needs.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:payload-isolation
rows.statement: Separate removable payload from retained structural commitment.

rows.label: case:necessity:payload-isolation-joint-commitment
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:payload-isolation``: Keep a bounded payload in a separable, concealing and removable commitment part; refuse committing structure and payload jointly, which makes payload removal prevent authentication of intact structural history and forces a choice between removal and integrity.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:pre-commitment-before-salting
rows.statement: Retain the actor-approved unsalted proposal before host enrichment.

rows.label: case:necessity:pre-commitment-before-salting-host-first
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:pre-commitment-before-salting``: Keep the Actor’s signed unsalted proposal pre-commitment before host salting; refuse host-first commitments with only a final Actor signature, which leave no cryptographic trace of endpoints, content or dependencies substituted before salting.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:approval-after-salting
rows.statement: Require actor approval of the final salted verified act.

rows.label: case:necessity:approval-after-salting-no-approval
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:approval-after-salting``: Keep Actor approval of the exact host-salted verified act before admission; refuse admitting a host-constructed verified act without that second signature, which binds the Actor to content or dependencies they never opened or checked.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:act-level-dependencies
rows.statement: Address dependencies to complete acts with one projection per act.

rows.label: case:necessity:act-level-dependencies-leg-dependencies
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:act-level-dependencies``: Keep dependencies at act level with one dependency projection and shared parent act for both hyper-edge legs; refuse separate per-leg lists and ordering, which can split an atomic act across another act or bind a provable dependency list to only one leg.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:authoritative-order
rows.statement: Publish one agreed total act order rather than independent local linearizations.

rows.label: case:necessity:authoritative-order-local-linearization
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:authoritative-order``: Keep one published authoritative total act order; refuse publishing only the accepted set and letting readers linearize locally, which makes raw maturities, projected times and path eligibility diverge. Standing remains set-based on its final-state inputs rather than using that residual order.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:retained-commitment
rows.statement: Retain dependency commitment residue after tombstoning.

rows.label: case:necessity:retained-commitment-remove-residue
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:retained-commitment``: Keep the binding dependency commitment residue after removing the list and opening; refuse deleting the residue too, which leaves a later fraud proof nothing to open against and permits fabricated lists or denial of the committed list.

rows.label: subsec:necessity:title-order-separation
rows.statement: Use authoritative order for handshake formation and epoch membership for conflict outcomes.

rows.label: case:necessity:title-order-separation-host-title-tiebreak
rows.statement: Refused simplification under ``subsec:necessity:title-order-separation``: Keep Bid-before-Accept-before-Ratify well-formedness under authoritative order while title conflict resolution reads epoch membership; refuse using residual sub-epoch host order to choose the winning commit, which gives the operator a title-fabrication lever.

rows.label: app:deployment
rows.statement: Track deployment as a separately addressable appendix.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:public-availability
rows.statement: Publish complete accepted act envelopes and edge projections with unrestricted availability.

rows.label: case:deployment:public-availability-streaming
rows.statement: Streaming the append-log through pub/sub satisfies public availability when every participant can retrieve the public act records, projections and standing-package data required for independent verification; streaming minimizes cache staleness.

rows.label: case:deployment:public-availability-api-polling
rows.statement: Open API polling with pagination is a public-availability option: it introduces bounded staleness without breaking the requirement that participants can retrieve the records and standing-package data needed for verification.

rows.label: case:deployment:public-availability-snapshot-delta
rows.statement: Periodic snapshots with delta encoding are a public-availability option: bounded staleness is permitted while participants retain access to the records and standing-package data needed for verification.

rows.label: case:deployment:public-availability-gossip
rows.statement: P2P gossip replication satisfies public availability when it makes the public records and required standing-package data continuously retrievable for independent verification.

rows.label: case:deployment:public-availability-gated-access
rows.statement: Gating read access to act envelopes or their edge projections violates public availability; a participant must not be confined to an arbitrary unreadable subset of the graph needed for verification.

rows.label: case:deployment:public-availability-through-creator
rows.statement: In the public-availability proof sketch, an absent path that would pass through the creator is indistinguishable in a gated view from one routed around the creator. The invisible path therefore prevents independent verification of that creator’s centrality.

rows.label: case:deployment:public-availability-around-creator
rows.statement: In the public-availability proof sketch, an absent path routed around the creator has the same visible symptom as one passing through the creator: neither is visible. Continuous access to the full published edge set removes this ambiguity.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:final-epoch-state-agreement
rows.statement: Agree on the complete final-marker package and authoritative accepted-act sequence; act order alone cannot determine the marker-accepted burn snapshot.

rows.label: case:deployment:final-epoch-state-agreement-linearization
rows.statement: Strict append-log linearization is a final-state agreement mechanism only if honest participants converge on the same authoritative order and complete epoch package.

rows.label: case:deployment:final-epoch-state-agreement-cluster-closure
rows.statement: Cluster-closure writes under the published closure rule are compliant only if honest participants converge on the same authoritative order and complete epoch package; ordered membership alone does not choose the accepted marker view.

rows.label: case:deployment:final-epoch-state-agreement-bft-finality
rows.statement: A BFT or finality gadget committing the ordered frontier is compliant only if honest participants converge on the same authoritative order and complete epoch package.

rows.label: case:deployment:final-epoch-state-agreement-gossip-stability
rows.statement: Gossip replication with stability depth is compliant only if honest participants converge on the same authoritative order and complete epoch package.

rows.label: case:deployment:final-epoch-state-agreement-disagreement
rows.statement: Disagreement between participants on the authoritative order fails final epoch state agreement; formation and order-sensitive raw quantities require that common order.

rows.label: case:deployment:final-epoch-state-agreement-inconsistent-projection
rows.statement: A projection, envelope or admission package not deterministically derived from the agreed complete epoch package fails agreement. Mixed histories, marker-policy editions or debit vintages, out-of-lineage burns, dropped predecessor acceptance, policy deviations and double-counted ancestry violate the package requirements.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:immutability
rows.statement: Preserve accepted record contents while permitting changes only to removable carriage.

rows.label: case:deployment:immutability-mutable-records
rows.statement: Mutable published edge records, including parameter updates, retroactive corrections and soft deletion, violate immutability: a retrieved record must remain valid for later replay rather than silently invalidating cached computations.

rows.label: post:deployment:public-object-replay
rows.statement: Determine normative identity and replay from public objects rather than hashes or digests.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:feed-reproducibility
rows.statement: Terminal feed reproduction obligations are recorded but no feed engine is proposed in Layer 1.

rows.label: case:deployment:feed-reproducibility-closed-form
rows.statement: The chosen deterministic closed-form feed formula permits clients to execute the full ranking computation without server state and avoids model-weight overhead; it must remain compatible with device-local computation.

rows.label: case:deployment:feed-reproducibility-public-model
rows.statement: A model with publicly distributed, locally executable weights can satisfy feed reproducibility in principle only if the client can execute the full computation without server state. Modern-scale weight storage and inference requirements conflict with the device-local invariant described here.

rows.label: case:deployment:feed-reproducibility-consensus-ranking
rows.statement: Consensus-computed ranking refreshed per epoch satisfies feed reproducibility only if a client can execute the full computation without server state.

rows.label: case:deployment:feed-reproducibility-opaque-model
rows.statement: Opaque server-held model weights inaccessible to clients fail feed reproducibility: clients cannot independently compute or falsify the claimed ranking.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:device-local
rows.statement: Keep device-local terminal computation outside the core scope and require published payload/workload/cache sizing with a declared rejection criterion.

rows.label: case:deployment:device-local-depth-four
rows.statement: The chosen feed depth four bounds the ego-network for device-local caching and computation without a per-request server dependency. Its exact value is calibrated against degree distributions; device-local scope is the invariant.

rows.label: case:deployment:device-local-depth-three
rows.statement: Feed depth three is an alternative depth bound subject to the same device-cacheability and no-per-request-server-dependency invariant; the exact depth is calibrated.

rows.label: case:deployment:device-local-depth-six
rows.statement: Feed depth six is subject to device-cacheability; at mean out-degree ten its million-node envelope needs gigabytes and server infrastructure for most devices, unlike the chosen depth four.

rows.label: case:deployment:device-local-server-assisted
rows.statement: Server-assisted feed computation beyond the local cache fails device-local scope when the client needs per-request graph data from the server whose ranking it is verifying.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas
rows.statement: Publish formula and constant editions and announce changes before they affect reproduction.

rows.label: case:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas-edition-fixed
rows.statement: The chosen protocol formulas and structural constants are immutable within a structural edition; changes require a publicly identified structural change with advance notice, not silent retuning.

rows.label: case:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas-scheduled-vote
rows.statement: Governance-vote updates are compatible with formula transparency only on a published schedule with enough lead time for clients to recompute affected cached values before the change applies.

rows.label: case:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas-time-locked
rows.statement: Time-locked update windows with independent oracle attestation are compatible with formula transparency only if clients cannot be surprised by silent changes; the declaration remains fixed within its structural edition.

rows.label: case:deployment:transparency-of-protocol-formulas-silent-tuning
rows.statement: Silent parameter changes invalidate cached values and accountability; publish changed formulas, reduced controller inputs and led outputs without repricing past debits. An aggregate source ceiling limits amount, not funded-partition allocation or strategic standing advantage. Identical public records cannot distinguish legitimate separation from strategic concentration under ``thm:epoch:split-observational-equivalence``; private purpose is not a record-derived input.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:calibration-declarations
rows.statement: Group the public standing, wall, boundary, encoding and replay declarations required before an edition takes effect.

rows.label: post:deployment:calibration-declarations
rows.statement: Publish the edition declarations before effect and retain all material needed to replay them; a reference may be used without claiming empirical optimality.

rows.label: cond:deployment:standing-parameters
rows.statement: Declare tilt profile/grid, normalized nonnegative depth masses and deepest support, positive self-retention, nonnegative domain weights and normalized family profiles with admissibility evidence; deepest positive depth incurs its full cumulative tilt. Deployment declares before effect; bite 2 carries declarations, bite 5 compiles them and bite 6 certifies them. Complete-act partitions can still change author-indexed folds and normalized rows; standing invariance needs additional premises. The all-state hop-intertwining premises of ``thm:dynamics:split-hop-refinement`` are a sufficient invariance criterion, not a consequence of act partition alone.

rows.label: cond:deployment:wall-calibration
rows.statement: Publish numeraire, policy floor, fixed structural floor with exact object, margin, controller edition/init/constants and total comparison procedure. Compare both chartered floors, neither a default; distinguish proposal from delivered wall and preserve debit vintage. Deployment supplies evidence; epoch bites 6 and 7 certify the charge and controller.

rows.label: cond:deployment:boundary-policy
rows.statement: Declare size and duration bounds, floor/announcement lead, candidate search/trial budget, timeout, availability target and fallback, plus a constant-change window freezing cadence retargeting. No unwritten candidate gains an admission right. Deployment owns policy; host bite 8 applies it with bite 7 validation.

rows.label: cond:deployment:canonical-encoding
rows.statement: Publish and version one canonical encoding with Actor/support order, rational representations, nonexact disclosures and all profile, depth, emission, controller and certificate fields; supply round-trip evidence. Host bite 8 encodes through pn-interchange; stored history retains exact package bytes and the effective encoding edition for replay bite 9. The paper selects no byte codec.

rows.label: cond:deployment:canonical-replay
rows.statement: Publish deterministic certification, precision, refinement, equality and stopping limits. The same inputs and procedure must reproduce every attempted PASS, FAIL or INDECISIVE verdict and greatest proved passing rung, with the exact anchor available. Threshold straddling refines or rejects; no tolerance chooses a verdict. Bites 6 and 8 publish the procedure and history, and replay bite 9 reconstructs its original edition and inputs. Declared fibres and matched comparison histories permit replay of pair displacement and projected residuals; common ownership and counterfactual histories remain explicit inputs rather than inferred record facts. The comparison inputs follow ``def:epoch:actor-partition-comparison`` and cannot distinguish private purpose between identical records under ``thm:epoch:split-observational-equivalence``.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:centralized-monitoring
rows.statement: Group required centralized certificate, emission, controller, work and cadence observations, without new binding feedback.

rows.label: post:deployment:centralized-monitoring
rows.statement: The centralized operator publishes reproducible observations, sampling, aggregation, thresholds, persistence, reviews and crossing dispositions; targets never waive exact standing, the floor, certification or input quarantine.

rows.label: cond:deployment:certificate-monitoring
rows.statement: The centralized operator publishes per-epoch fence, width, rung, enclosure radius, movement, hop mass and below-wall fraction; aggregate FAIL versus INDECISIVE, fallback frequencies, thresholds, persistence and crossing reviews. Screen failure is not certificate failure. Epoch bite 6 supplies evidence, host bite 8 publishes it, and deployment owns monitoring. For partition comparisons identify fibre, matched histories, rungs, pair shock, mixture variation and residual bound; distinguish identities from measured displacement without adding a gate or ownership inference. The comparison measures the displacement bounded by ``prop:epoch:split-pair-displacement``.

rows.label: cond:deployment:emission-experience
rows.statement: The operator publishes wall, emission and exported-pair distributions, sag and rehabilitation with source rates, rung, interval and changed supports; declare thresholds, persistence, review and response. Report the export cap without a small-movement guarantee; no observation adds controller inputs or silently changes emission. Epoch bites 5 and 6 supply fields, host bite 8 publishes, and deployment owns comparisons. For declared funded partitions report actual export beside both fibre ceilings, Registration debit beside incremental burn, and maximum-standing concentration; the same concentration exposure can measure a legitimately separate role under ``ex:epoch:split-showcase``.

rows.label: cond:deployment:controller-performance
rows.statement: Publish plant/activity/burn hypotheses, tested range and tracking, error, settling and chatter including failures; include price, capacity, emission and below-wall fractions. Declare review criteria for step and deadband calibration; failures authorize neither escalation nor new inputs nor unconditional tracking claims. Epoch bite 7 supplies controller results, host bite 8 publishes, and deployment owns trials.

rows.label: cond:deployment:standing-work
rows.statement: Measure per epoch/trial edges, support, width, clearance, SCCs, passes, residuals, invalidations and elapsed time against declared workload, hardware, arithmetic and memory envelopes; report missed targets and use declared fallback without dropping relations or approximating standing. Bites 6, 7 and 11 supply scoped work evidence; deployment owns operational percentile publication.

rows.label: cond:deployment:cadence-maturity
rows.statement: The deployment measures raw maturity drift and terminal observations when boundary timing changes, publishes adaptation-window freeze evidence and threshold responses. Raw maturity never becomes a projected-standing input. Host bite 8 publishes boundary facts and readouts bite 10 supplies the optional raw service; terminal-consumer computation remains a deployment duty under (`open:inventory:deployment-terminal-evidence`).

rows.label: subsec:deployment:calibration-evidence
rows.statement: Group deployment comparison and conformance evidence, not new universal constants.

rows.label: post:deployment:calibration-evidence
rows.statement: Publish exact inputs or acquisition procedure, editions, workload, method, predeclared criteria, results and limitations; report failed criteria without changing the comparison after seeing it.

rows.label: cond:deployment:parameter-comparisons
rows.statement: Publish baseline/candidate inputs, affected derived values, criteria and regenerated evidence for structural parameter changes. Keep temperature fixed absent charter adoption; recompute tier, discovery and margin comparisons, and distinguish recoinage from structural migration without holding standing fixed. Bites 6, 7, 10 and 11 furnish relevant fixtures; deployment owns criteria, terminal comparisons and review, with no hidden controller feedback.

rows.label: cond:deployment:payload-cache-envelope
rows.statement: Publish payload cap, indexing/encoding overhead, cache budget, traversal/depth-four envelope, parallel complete-act workload and retention horizon. Count one allowance per authored act and none for derived edges; reject oversized candidate workload/cap combinations. Deployment owns capacity sizing; records validation and host bite 8 support declared bounds, while terminal cache computation stays held under (`open:inventory:deployment-terminal-evidence`).

rows.label: cond:deployment:boundary-search-evidence
rows.statement: Publish trials and elapsed envelopes with dependencies, insolvency, safety, headroom, registration/vouch and title-conflict cases; declare hardware, arithmetic, residual, timeout and fallback. Reuse must reproduce certified outputs and revalidate changed inputs. Bites 7, 8 and 11 supply validator/host comparisons; deployment publishes findings without claiming optimal selection or complete unwritten demand.

rows.label: cond:deployment:terminal-regression
rows.statement: For each standing-edition change, publish consumer-specific inputs, deltas, fit/tolerance and failure response using actual dependencies; insulated CAN does not thereby read standing. Readouts bite 10 and corpus bite 11 cover the supported raw surface; other terminal comparisons belong to deployments under (`open:inventory:deployment-terminal-evidence`).

rows.label: cond:deployment:complete-act-conformance
rows.statement: Publish compiler/replay evidence for parallel authored acts, identities, folds, revocations, recipient resolution, domain profiles and allocation under original ledger/threshold vintages. Reproduce the accepted-act census; source inspection or a certificate on incomplete projections is insufficient. Bites 3 through 6 build the semantics, replay bite 9 reconstructs them and bite 11 composes the evidence.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:sufficiency
rows.statement: Require sufficient public edge and parent-act data to reconstruct every binding graph quantity.

rows.label: case:deployment:sufficiency-minimal-record
rows.statement: The chosen minimal sufficient record permits independent recomputation from published parameters, temporal attributes, author and endpoints. Hyper-edge legs also carry role and reciprocal co-leg identity, and derived edges add no record fields.

rows.label: case:deployment:sufficiency-precomputed-record
rows.statement: An extended record may publish precomputed derived quantities for client convenience, such as cached temporal entropy, provided clients can recompute and verify them from the public sufficient record.

rows.label: case:deployment:sufficiency-redundant-record
rows.statement: Additional verified but redundant fields preserve record sufficiency because clients can recompute them; the server must not depend on unpublished enrichment.

rows.label: case:deployment:sufficiency-proprietary-fields
rows.statement: Proprietary fields on which the server’s scoring depends are not a valid sufficient-record implementation: every load-bearing input must be published for independent recomputation.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:concealment-entropy
rows.statement: Declare adequate concealment entropy for custody phases without inventing an entropy source.

rows.label: case:deployment:concealment-entropy-operator-generated
rows.statement: In the centralized phase, operator-generated concealment values under audit are compliant only if low-entropy generation is detectable or precluded before concealment is relied on; the operator owns that obligation.

rows.label: case:deployment:concealment-entropy-client-generated
rows.statement: Client-side concealment-value generation is compliant against a published entropy specification validated at append, only if low-entropy generation is detectable or precluded before concealment is relied on.

rows.label: case:deployment:concealment-entropy-secret-derived
rows.statement: Deterministic concealment-value derivation from a client secret is compliant under a published rule only if low-entropy generation is detectable or precluded before concealment is relied on.

rows.label: case:deployment:concealment-entropy-unassigned-custody
rows.statement: Leaving concealment-entropy custody unassigned in the decentralized phase fails the obligation: a published generation rule must bind the carriage layer before concealment is relied on.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility
rows.statement: Verify marker policy, lineage, accepted-set bounds and distinct destructions before rebuilding the ledger, compiler inputs, rung attempts, certificates, standing and gates.

rows.label: case:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility-reference-compiler
rows.statement: The chosen deterministic reference compiler and independently executable certificate tools must replay act reconstruction, folds, allocation, emission, certificate evaluation and mediant convergence from public inputs.

rows.label: case:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility-formal-compiler
rows.statement: A machine-checked formal compiler is an alternative for conserved-standing reproduction only with the same outputs from the published inputs; implementation variation requires a formula/compiler edition change under the no-silent-change rule.

rows.label: case:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility-equivalent-compiler
rows.statement: Another conserved-standing implementation is permitted only with the same outputs from published inputs; implementation variation requires a formula/compiler edition change under the no-silent-change rule.

rows.label: case:deployment:conserved-standing-reproducibility-mismatched-package
rows.statement: A safe-looking projection, base matrix, emission diagonal or verdict fails reproduction if it omits accepted records, differs from deterministic allocation, concerns another standing point or does not match final standing; isolated validity is insufficient.

rows.label: prop:deployment:allocation-input-completeness
rows.statement: Ensure the standing compiler is deterministic over the disclosed accepted-act and ledger inputs.

rows.label: rem:deployment:completeness-safety-orthogonal
rows.statement: Check compiler completeness separately from numerical safety certification.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:canonical-standing-encoding
rows.statement: Declare canonical actor order, numeric representations and certificate encodings.

rows.label: post:deployment:canonical-standing-publication
rows.statement: Publish the full canonical standing package and attempted-rung verdicts under one versioned encoding and deterministic certification procedure; value allowances cannot excuse different certificate verdicts, including INDECISIVE. Partition comparisons require explicit fibres and matched histories; the record establishes neither common control nor the alternative history. The comparison inputs follow ``def:epoch:actor-partition-comparison`` and cannot distinguish private purpose between identical records under ``thm:epoch:split-observational-equivalence``.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:terminal-centrality-certificates
rows.statement: Terminal centrality certificate publication does not introduce a Layer 1 centrality engine.

rows.label: case:deployment:terminal-centrality-certificates-tree-samples
rows.statement: Published Dijkstra-tree samples are the chosen terminal-centrality certificate: any participant can independently reproduce a creator’s centrality within the published approximation bounds without a trusted intermediary.

rows.label: case:deployment:terminal-centrality-certificates-selective-reveal
rows.statement: A commitment with per-creator selective reveal lets a creator verify their own centrality but not others’, weakening collective auditing compared with published Dijkstra-tree samples.

rows.label: case:deployment:terminal-centrality-certificates-auditor
rows.statement: Third-party auditor attestation of terminal centrality reintroduces a trusted intermediary; the chosen published-tree method instead permits every participant to run the computation independently.

rows.label: case:deployment:terminal-centrality-certificates-scalar-only
rows.statement: Publishing only centrality scalars while suppressing sampled Dijkstra-path trees fails participant verification: the approximation error remains a server claim rather than an independently measured quantity.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation
rows.statement: CAN enrichment stays outside binding Layer 1 standing and gates.

rows.label: case:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation-frobenius
rows.statement: Pure attribution-view Frobenius norms are the chosen CAN enrichment inputs. No path-view or standing-derived quantity enters the recursion, and normalized enrichment is independent of an actor’s standing when that actor’s Declaration is outside its own dependency closure.

rows.label: case:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation-standing-scaled
rows.statement: A standing-scaled CAN enrichment component is rejected: it introduces standing dependence and counts the influence signal again alongside the reward formula’s existing amplifier.

rows.label: case:deployment:can-enrichment-insulation-path-corrected
rows.statement: A path-view determinant correction in CAN enrichment is rejected: it introduces path-view tier discrimination into attribution rather than preserving the attribution-view recursion.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:completeness
rows.statement: Disclose every binding formula and policy input needed to reproduce the deployed boundary.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-written-specification
rows.statement: A complete normative written specification is the chosen publication form: it must determine every binding computation and each terminal computation a guild elects to publish, with no proprietary load-bearing component.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-source-implementation
rows.statement: An open-source reference implementation is an alternative publication form only when complete enough to reproduce every binding computation and each terminal computation a guild elects to publish.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-formal-specification
rows.statement: A machine-checked formal specification with test vectors is an alternative complete publication form; vectors disambiguate mask promotion, bleed-softening boundaries and raw parity relaxation, without replacing the requirement for completeness.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-missing-constants
rows.statement: Publishing formula structure without constants fails completeness: participants cannot reproduce all binding outputs and the terminal outputs a guild elects to publish.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-missing-promotion
rows.statement: Publishing constants without mask-promotion criteria fails completeness: the published information must determine the promoted masks used in computation.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-missing-epoch
rows.statement: Publishing promotion criteria without epoch architecture fails completeness: the published information must also determine the boundary computation.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-unpublished-masks
rows.statement: In the formula-completeness proof sketch, unpublished mask-promotion criteria leave promoted-edge determinant scores underspecified, and the per-edge error multiplies along paths containing promoted edges.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-unpublished-can
rows.statement: In the formula-completeness proof sketch, an unpublished CAN recursion leaves the normalized enrichment factor uncomputable and the reward formula opaque at its attribution-view bridge.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-unpublished-epoch
rows.statement: In the formula-completeness proof sketch, unpublished boundary architecture leaves write budget, liveness window and burn snapshot undefined; different boundary assumptions yield different standing and unverifiable participation decisions.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-unpublished-parity
rows.statement: In the formula-completeness proof sketch, an unpublished parity relaxation rule prevents verification of raw positive-parity paths. This requirement applies only to raw signed services publishing such results; standing instead requires its initiator-owned package.

rows.label: case:deployment:completeness-unpublished-standing
rows.statement: In the formula-completeness proof sketch, unpublished standing projection or certificate computation allows identical accepted edges to produce inconsistent standing claims. A final scalar or verdict alone cannot bind completeness, the base matrix and the accepted rung; the entire conserved standing package is needed.

rows.label: subsec:deployment:realization-obligations
rows.statement: Publish the dimensioned positive unit cost and separate event costs, bootstrap bound, settlement depth and finality, provenance, applicable operator proof or explained absence, and fixed marker policy with complete acceptance evidence.

rows.label: case:deployment:realization-obligations-pointer
rows.statement: A pointer to the realization’s own publication is a compliant carriage mechanism only if participants can obtain its published quantities through the network at any time and compare them with the realization’s publication.

rows.label: case:deployment:realization-obligations-mirror
rows.statement: Mirroring the realization’s publication in the network append-log is compliant only if participants can obtain the quantities at any time and compare them with the original publication; carriage must not silently alter them.

rows.label: case:deployment:realization-obligations-snapshot
rows.statement: Periodic snapshots of the realization’s read constants alongside network constants are compliant only if participants can obtain and compare them with the realization’s published quantities at any time.

rows.label: case:deployment:realization-obligations-withheld-evidence
rows.statement: A realization withholding audit quantities, capacity bound, unit cost or settlement depth does not meet the burn interface; the network cannot replace missing provenance with its own assertion.

rows.label: case:deployment:realization-obligations-occlusion
rows.statement: A deployment must not occlude, restate or silently alter the realization’s published quantities: participants must be able to compare carriage with the original evidence rather than audit only the network’s assertion.
